newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says to challenge U.S. cement dumping move.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says to challenge U.S. cement dumping move.

text.p: Mexico's deputy trade minister Jaime Zabludovsky said on Friday that Mexico was "very dissatisfied" and planned to complain to the U.S. Commerce Department over its decision to raise dumping tariffs on Mexican cement imports.

The U.S. Commerce Department decided on Thursday to raise the taxes charged on Mexican cement to 103.8 percent, compared with a current rate of 62 percent. The hike was after the fifth review of dumping charges in the long-standing trade dispute.

"Clearly we are very unsatisfied with the investigation's results...and in the coming weeks we will continue to be in contact with the Mexican industry and with the U.S. authorities to make them aware of our disagreement," Zabludovsky told reporters at a meeting with Spanish business leaders.

The U.S. decision applies to cement imports from Mexico during the period from August 1994 to July 1995. The dumping charges accuse Mexican cement firms of exporting the product at prices below those in its domestic market.
Analysts have estimated the anti-dumping tariff cost Mexican firms $23.7 million during the time period.
Grupos Cementos Chihuahua (GCC) and Cemex are the Mexican cement companies most targeted in the U.S. dumping case, which began in 1988 at the instigation of U.S. firms.
